text: MIXED: GSEA of label-free proteomics showed the proton transmembrane transport pathway enriched in APOE4 vs APOE2 iAstrocytes (padj<0.2). In APOE4 vs APOE3 the pathway was not significantly enriched (pale bar, near zero). The authors interpret this as a possible compensatory change related to V-ATPase-driven lysosomal acidification; no pH was measured.
description: Human iPSC-derived astrocytes (iAstrocytes, day 44, quiescent after AraC and FCS withdrawal) from EBiSC isogenic lines BIONi010-C-4 (APOE4), -C-2 (APOE3), -C-6 (APOE2). Baseline, untreated. Label-free MS proteomics with fgsea GSEA on moderated t-statistics; 3 biological replicates per genotype. Caveat: iPSC-derived, not primary brain astrocytes. Pathway enrichment of proton transport proteins is a weak surrogate for endosomal pH and is not compartment-specific.

provenance.excerpt: Proton and cation transmembrane transport were highest in APOE4 iAstrocytes, and lowest in E2 (Figure 4A).

meccogFinding.summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (proton transmembrane transport proteome pathway not significantly changed vs E3; increased vs E2) -> [inferred] altered endolysosomal acidification machinery [NO EFFECT vs APOE3]

perturbed.variable: APOE genotype (isogenic APOE4 vs APOE3 vs APOE2 iPSC-astrocytes)
